edges.sentence: so my name is rima vatra i am a medical oncologist hematologist and i treat all cancer types i see blood disorders one of the most common cancers i see and treat is breast cancer [Music] it was a busy time of the year it's always very busy at work and i had to do my mammogram so i thought i would be in and out in 20 minutes like i always had been but this time was different after the mammogram was done on the first pass the radiologist came in and asked me to do ultrasounds of both sides and on that ultrasound is where they found a tumor and this is when i started to worry a little bit [Music] at the time of the diagnosis my kids were seven about to be eight um so i had to tell them things in a simple way i didn't tell them right away because the day i found out was december 23rd so i didn't want to ruin christmas after we went through those festivities i did sit them down and i explained that i would need surgery because i was sick the biopsy was initially an invasive ductal carcinoma and a very slow-growing appearing tumor so it was a very favorable looking tumor to begin with but you don't know your stage until after your surgery because i was diagnosed at such an early early stage i didn't need a big surgery um and so my recovery from that was very fast and i didn't need chemo so my kids never really saw me looking like i was going through something very severe and i'm glad i'm glad for that [Music] i can 100 say the mammogram saved my life we are such busy women we have we take care of families we have work we have social lives we have hobbies make time for your medical care because it can change the entire course of your life in just a matter of 30 minutes [Music]

10-year survival with prostate cancer is 98% 15 years survival with prostate cancer is 94% now those numbers are going to be better going forward you can't have 15-year outcomes without going 15 years certain rare subtypes of prostate cancer that behave much more aggressively and those are the ones we all hear about the bad news stories so men with prostate cancer need to be very careful about defining what type of prostate cancer they have most of the prostate cancers are very manageable curable and can be controlled for very long periods of time so survival rates with prostate cancer are surprisingly good and of course with modern medicine they're getting even better men who are facing a new diagnosis of prostate cancer since survival is so excellent need to be considering how their treatment is going to impact their quality of life they're going to live with these treatment decisions for many many years many people rush into therapy thinking that fight the cancer aggressively get cured I don't want to die and that type of attitude is typically entirely appropriate for people with other types of cancers with prostate cancer because that the prostate is located in such a sensitive area very near the issues of urinary function and sexual function men need to be a little more circumspect go a little more slowly and look at the whole broad spectrum because thankfully survival rates with prostate cancer in general are really really good [Music] [Applause]
